title: SceneDiffuser: Efficient and Controllable Driving Simulation Initialization and Rollout

control_signal.value: Inpainting masks over the scene tensor (conditioning on chosen agents, timesteps, feature channels), generalized hard constraints (non-collision, range, on-road), and constraint specifications for injected agents written by an LLM from text.

control_mechanism.value: Multi-task inpainting with randomized control masks during training; hard constraints applied at inference after each diffusion step; few-shot prompted LLM generates constraint protos from natural language.

base_model.value: Scene-level diffusion transformer: Perceiver IO global context encoder, spatiotemporal transformer denoiser with AdaLN conditioning, amortized autoregressive rollout, 16 denoising steps.

datasets.value: Waymo Open Motion Dataset (WOMD), used for scene generation and for the Waymo Open Sim Agents Challenge (WOSAC) rollout evaluation.

metrics.value: WOSAC realism composite metric and components (kinematics, collision, TTC, offroad, distance to objects); collision and offroad rates; ADE and minADE; scene-generation distributional realism buckets; number of function evaluations.

controllability_evidence.value: Hard collision constraints raise scene-generation composite realism from 0.516 to 0.558 and collision score from 0.692 to 0.841. LLM-constraint scene generation of long-tail agents succeeded in 40/100 manually judged samples.

stated_limitations.value: Does not exceed SOTA of other autoregressive models; validity masks are not modelled and logged validity is used instead.

notes: Multiple control routes; labelled inference-time guidance because the abstract names hard constraints as the inference-time mechanism, but inpainting masks and LLM prompting are also used. Controllability numbers for 40/100 come from an appendix qualitative judgement of four prototype constraint types (25 each).
